description: Author the fork-local BMAD building-block dataset as committed markdown files that mirror the upstream awslabs/aidlc-workflows core/** frontmatter shapes, so they map cleanly through the SAME shared/block-mappers.js mappers the aidlc-v2 baseline uses. This feature produces ONLY the data (markdown files) + a small index/loader; the seed-path wiring and tests are FEAT-003. All ids are kebab-case and namespaced `bmad-*` (blocks) / `bmad` (workflow) so they never collide with or shadow the upstream `aidlc-*` SYSTEM ids. Model the BMAD 6.10.0 workshop flow (Phases 0-6) as faithfully as the 9 block types allow. Do NOT model the batch/loop runner (run_loop.py / KiroCrew) — the user explicitly excluded it.
steps: Create a fork-local dataset dir mirroring the upstream layout so the existing mappers parse it unchanged: lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/core/<same subdirs as upstream>. The mappers key off path prefixes: stages under core/aidlc-common/stages/<phase>/, agents under core/agents/, scopes under core/scopes/, rules under core/rules/, skills under core/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md, templates under core/templates/, knowledge under core/knowledge/<agentDir>/. Study lambda/shared/test/fixtures/repo-files.js for the EXACT frontmatter shape of each block type before authoring.

AGENTS (core/agents/): author the BMAD roles as Agent blocks with frontmatter {name: bmad-<role>-agent, display_name, description, tier}. Roles: bmad-pm-agent (PM/John, tier judgment), bmad-architect-agent (Architect/Winston, tier judgment), bmad-ux-agent (UX designer, tier balanced), bmad-dev-agent (Dev, tier balanced), bmad-tea-agent (Test Architect/Murat, tier judgment), bmad-party-mode-agent (collaborative multi-persona reviewer, tier judgment), and reviewer agents used as stage reviewers: bmad-architecture-reviewer-agent (tier judgment) and bmad-prd-reviewer-agent (tier judgment). Body = a short persona description grounded in the doc (PM owns PRD; Architect owns ARCHITECTURE-SPINE + component→file ownership table + persistence design; UX owns DESIGN.md + EXPERIENCE.md; TEA/Murat owns test strategy, framework gating, ATDD; party-mode convenes 3-5 personas).

SCOPES (core/scopes/): author two Scope blocks modeling the two BMAD paths. brownfield: core/scopes/bmad-brownfield.md {name: bmad-brownfield, depth: Comprehensive, description, keywords}. greenfield: core/scopes/bmad-greenfield.md {name: bmad-greenfield, depth: Comprehensive, description, keywords}. Per the doc the two paths differ in exactly 4 places (1.1 skipped in greenfield; 1.2 -> 1.2g; 3.8 constitution back-fill only in greenfield; 4.2 framework is a hard first-story requirement in greenfield). These differences are expressed via each stage's `scopes` frontmatter (which scope(s) execute the stage) — see the STAGES step. depth must be one of Minimal|Standard|Comprehensive (shared/blocks.js DEPTHS).

STAGES (core/aidlc-common/stages/<phase>/): author one Stage per BMAD step, using PHASE_ORDER buckets [initialization, ideation, inception, construction, operation]. Map BMAD phases onto these: Phase 0 install -> initialization; Phase 1 prep + Phase 2 planning -> ideation; Phase 3 architecture/stories + Phase 4 test design -> inception; Phase 5 dev loop -> construction; Phase 6 wrap-up + 5.9 regression -> operation. Each stage frontmatter follows mapStage: {slug: bmad-<step>, name, number (display e.g. '1.1'), phase, execution: ALWAYS|CONDITIONAL, condition, lead_agent, support_agents[], mode: inline, produces[], optional_produces[], consumes[{artifact, required, conditional_on?}], requires_stage[], sensors[], reviewer?, reviewer_max_iterations?, scopes[]}. Author these stages (slug -> phase -> scopes -> notes): bmad-document-project (ideation, scopes:[bmad-brownfield] ONLY — greenfield skips 1.1; lead bmad-architect-agent; produces system-map/tech-stack/api-contracts/feature-domains), bmad-generate-project-context (ideation, scopes:[bmad-brownfield]; lead bmad-architect-agent; produces project-context; models the 'project constitution' from existing code — persistent_facts/protected paths), bmad-generate-project-context-greenfield (ideation, scopes:[bmad-greenfield], number 1.2; produces project-context; first-pass tech-agnostic constitution with [decided]/[await-architecture] annotations), bmad-prd (ideation, scopes:[both], lead bmad-pm-agent, reviewer bmad-prd-reviewer-agent reviewer_max_iterations 2, consumes project-context optional, produces prd), bmad-ux (ideation, execution CONDITIONAL condition 'run when the initiative has a UI', scopes:[both], lead bmad-ux-agent, consumes prd required, produces design-spine + experience-spine, note runs parallel with architecture), bmad-architecture (inception, scopes:[both], lead bmad-architect-agent, reviewer bmad-architecture-reviewer-agent reviewer_max_iterations 2, consumes prd required + design-spine optional conditional_on ui + experience-spine optional conditional_on ui, produces architecture-spine + component-file-ownership + persistence-design), bmad-spec (inception, execution CONDITIONAL, scopes:[both], lead bmad-architect-agent, consumes architecture-spine + prd, produces spec), bmad-party-mode-architecture-review (inception, execution CONDITIONAL, scopes:[both], lead bmad-party-mode-agent, consumes architecture-spine, produces architecture-review-notes; the 3.3 architecture party-mode gate), bmad-create-epics-and-stories (inception, scopes:[both], lead bmad-pm-agent, consumes prd + architecture-spine + spec optional, produces epics-and-stories with per-story file-ownership line), bmad-testarch-test-design (inception, scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes prd + architecture-spine, produces test-strategy + acceptance-framework-plan; note may run parallel with story creation), bmad-backfill-project-context (inception, scopes:[bmad-greenfield] ONLY — the 3.8 second-pass constitution back-fill, greenfield-only per doc; lead bmad-architect-agent, consumes architecture-spine + project-context, produces project-context), bmad-sprint-planning (inception, scopes:[both], lead bmad-pm-agent, consumes epics-and-stories, produces sprint-status; note: readiness check + story status tracking, NOT time-boxed sprints), bmad-testarch-framework (construction, execution CONDITIONAL condition 'gate-first: acceptance framework must be initialized before the first UI story', scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes acceptance-framework-plan, produces acceptance-framework; note for greenfield this is a hard first-story requirement, for brownfield often already present), bmad-create-story (construction, mode inline, for_each unit-of-work if the schema supports per-unit — otherwise plain inline, scopes:[both], lead bmad-pm-agent, consumes epics-and-stories + sprint-status, produces story), bmad-testarch-atdd (construction, scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes story + acceptance-framework, produces acceptance-tests-red; note: red-first, before dev-story), bmad-dev-story (construction, scopes:[both], lead bmad-dev-agent, consumes story + acceptance-tests-red + project-context, produces implementation + unit-tests, requires_stage bmad-testarch-atdd), bmad-code-review (construction, scopes:[both], lead bmad-dev-agent OR a reviewer agent, consumes implementation, produces code-review-findings; note: AI findings + severities are 'to be verified' — reproduce high-severity with a minimal test first), bmad-party-mode-consistency-review (construction, execution CONDITIONAL, scopes:[both], lead bmad-party-mode-agent, consumes implementation + prd + architecture-spine, produces consistency-review-notes; the 5.5 PRD<->impl<->arch consistency gate), bmad-e2e-regression (operation, execution CONDITIONAL condition 'run when the initiative has a UI; once, after all epics', scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes acceptance-framework + implementation, produces e2e-evidence), bmad-sprint-status (operation, scopes:[both], lead bmad-pm-agent, consumes sprint-status, produces sprint-status-report), bmad-retrospective (operation, execution CONDITIONAL, scopes:[both], lead bmad-party-mode-agent, consumes implementation, produces retrospective-notes), bmad-testarch-nfr (operation, execution CONDITIONAL, scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes implementation + test-strategy, produces nfr-assessment), bmad-testarch-trace (operation, scopes:[both], lead bmad-tea-agent, consumes epics-and-stories + e2e-evidence optional + nfr-assessment optional, produces traceability-matrix + release-decision). Ensure produces/consumes artifact names are consistent across stages so buildArtifacts and topologicalStageOrder wire a clean DAG (no cycles, no orphaned consumes). Keep each stage body short but faithful (2-8 lines) citing the BMAD step intent.

SKILLS (core/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md): the BMAD steps map 1:1 to user-invocable /bmad-* runners in the doc, so also author Skill blocks for the user-invocable ones. Frontmatter follows mapSkill: {name: bmad-<step>, description, argument-hint, user-invocable: true, classification}. Author skills for: bmad-document-project, bmad-generate-project-context, bmad-prd, bmad-ux, bmad-architecture, bmad-spec, bmad-party-mode, bmad-create-epics-and-stories, bmad-sprint-planning, bmad-create-story, bmad-testarch-framework, bmad-testarch-test-design, bmad-testarch-atdd, bmad-dev-story, bmad-code-review, bmad-sprint-status, bmad-retrospective, bmad-testarch-nfr, bmad-testarch-trace, bmad-agent-tea (the TEA agent entry point). classification e.g. 'read-only' for scanning/review/trace skills, 'write' for generative ones — keep consistent with the SKILL validation (userInvocable boolean, classification string).

TEMPLATES (core/templates/): author Template blocks for the authored scaffolds the doc references: bmad-project-context (the project constitution / guardrail doc with the 7 sections + persistent_facts + protected-paths list), bmad-project-context-greenfield (the greenfield first-pass template with [decided]/[await-architecture] annotations), bmad-prd (PRD scaffold with FR/AC sections), bmad-architecture-spine (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE with the mandatory component->file ownership table + persistence design sections), bmad-design-spine (DESIGN.md), bmad-experience-spine (EXPERIENCE.md), bmad-sprint-status (the sprint-status.yaml scaffold). Templates carry frontmatter {description} + a markdown/scaffold body (mapTemplate uses id from filename, description from frontmatter).

RULES (core/rules/): model BMAD's guardrail mechanism as Rule blocks. Rule files carry NO frontmatter — the mapper derives layer from the filename (bmad-org|bmad-team|bmad-project -> that layer; bmad-phase-<phase> -> phase layer). NOTE the mapper strips a leading `aidlc-` prefix for the derived id but keys layer off the base name after that strip; to get clean bmad-namespaced rule ids that still resolve to valid layers, confirm behavior against mapRule in block-mappers.js and the RULE_LAYERS enum in blocks.js during authoring, and choose filenames so the derived {layer, id} both validate (layer in org|team|project|phase). Author at minimum: a project-layer rule capturing the protected-paths / byte-frozen-baseline / 'backend is the authorization boundary, UI gating != security' guardrails, and phase-layer rules for the construction phase (ATDD red-first; high-severity findings must be reproduced with a minimal test before fixing) and inception phase (component->file ownership table required for parallel stories; existing DB is a higher-tier protected asset than code). Give each rule a body grounded in the doc's guardrail themes (project-context.md as persistent facts, protected paths, frozen contracts).

KNOWLEDGE (optional, core/knowledge/<agentDir>/): if time allows, attach a short methodology-knowledge doc to the TEA and architect agents (e.g. core/knowledge/bmad-tea-agent/test-architecture-principles.md, core/knowledge/bmad-architect-agent/brownfield-guardrails.md). No frontmatter; agentRef/doc derive from the path. This is a nice-to-have, not required for a faithful minimal model.

Add a tiny loader index: lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/index.js that exports the fork-local dataset as a Map<path, content> in the SAME shape fetchCoreFiles returns (repo-relative path -> file content string). Because the seed lambda is esbuild-bundled and runs without network access to a bmad repo, the dataset must be importable/bundled. Prefer generating the Map by importing the markdown as strings (e.g. read the files at bundle time via a small build step, OR inline them as a JS module of string literals). Choose the approach that esbuild bundles cleanly for node24 ESM (the seed-blocks build command is `esbuild index.js --bundle --platform=node ... --external:@aws-sdk/*`). Document the chosen approach in FEAT-002 findings so FEAT-003 wires it correctly.

Do NOT create any Sensor blocks unless a BMAD step maps to a deterministic post-stage command check; the doc's checks (shasum freeze verification, E2E green) are deterministic and MAY be modeled as Sensor blocks IF you can supply a real command + matches per mapSensor/validateBlockInput (a sensor requires a `command`). If you cannot supply a faithful command, OMIT sensors and record in findings that BMAD's freeze/E2E checks were modeled as Rules + stage reviewer gates instead of Sensors (acceptable — sensors need an executable script the fork does not have).
acceptance_criteria: A committed dataset under lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/core/** with markdown files for BMAD agents, scopes, stages, skills, templates, and rules, plus lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/index.js exporting a Map<path, content>.
Every authored id is kebab-case and prefixed bmad- (blocks) or is exactly `bmad` (the workflow, authored in FEAT-003); no id collides with an aidlc-* id.

Running the authored dataset through buildFromFiles(datasetMap) in a scratch node script (or the FEAT-003 test) yields blocks whose fields satisfy shared/blocks.js validateBlockInput(type, block) and validateId(block.id) for every block, and the derived artifact graph has no consumes referencing an artifact no stage produces.

Brownfield vs greenfield differences are represented purely via stage `scopes` frontmatter (1.1 + 1.2 brownfield-only; 1.2g + 3.8 back-fill greenfield-only; framework gating), not by duplicating stages.
The batch/loop runner is NOT modeled anywhere in the dataset.
verification: node -e "import('./lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/index.js').then(async m=>{const {buildFromFiles}=await import('./lambda/shared/block-mappers.js');const {validateBlockInput,validateId}=await import('./lambda/shared/blocks.js');const files=m.default?.CORE_FILES??m.CORE_FILES??m.default??m.datasetFiles; /* adjust to actual export */ })" — i.e. author a scratch validation (final assertion lives in FEAT-003 test) confirming every produced block validates
grep -rL 'bmad' lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/core || true  (spot-check ids are namespaced)
npm run format:check and npm run lint stay clean on the new files

findings.loader_export_shape: lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/index.js exports a Map<repoRelativePath, fileContentString> named CORE_FILES (and the same Map as the object `default.CORE_FILES`), IDENTICAL in shape to what shared/repo-fetch.js fetchCoreFiles returns, so it feeds straight into buildFromFiles(files) with no adapter. FEAT-003 should import it as: `import { CORE_FILES } from './bmad/index.js';` (or `bmadDataset.default.CORE_FILES`). The 65 markdown files under lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/core/** are the single source of truth; index.js imports each as a string via import attributes `import x from './core/....md' with { type: 'text' }` and assembles the Map. VERIFIED: esbuild inlines every `type: text` import as a string literal at bundle time with the EXACT seed-blocks build flags (`esbuild <abs>/index.js --bundle --platform=node --target=node24 --format=esm --external:@aws-sdk/*`) -> a 72KB self-contained bundle, no fs/network at runtime. NOTE for whoever runs esbuild by hand: pass the ABSOLUTE path to index.js (npx esbuild resolves a bare/`./` entry relative to the npx temp cwd, which silently bundled the WRONG entry in testing); the package.json `build` script's relative `index.js` is correct because npm runs it with cwd=the workspace dir.

unmappable_concepts.RULE ids cannot be bmad- prefixed AND la: mapRule derives {layer,id} from the filename: it strips ONLY a leading `aidlc-` then reads the base as the layer (org|team|project or phase-<x>). A `bmad-project.md` yields layer `bmad-project` which FAILS validateBlockInput (RULE_LAYERS). Since block-mappers.js is shared with the aidlc-v2 baseline and MUST NOT be modified, I could not get both a bmad- prefix and a valid layer. RESOLUTION (per FEAT-002 step 11 / the orchestrator's 'closest legitimate type' guidance): I prioritized the MANDATORY validation criterion + no-collision, naming the rule files with bare layer tokens (core/rules/project.md, phase-inception.md, phase-construction.md). These produce valid layers and ids (`project`, `phase-inception`, `phase-construction`) that do NOT collide with any upstream aidlc-* id (upstream keeps its full `aidlc-` prefix as the id, e.g. `aidlc-project`), and land in distinct blocks-table keys (BLOCK#SYSTEM#RULE#project vs BLOCK#SYSTEM#RULE#aidlc-project) and distinct workflow RULEREF rows in distinct WF#SYSTEM#bmad vs WF#SYSTEM#aidlc-v2 partitions. So the bmad namespace stays separate even though these 3 RULE ids are not literally `bmad-` prefixed. FEAT-003's bmad workflow builder should reference these rules by their derived {layer, id}. If strict bmad- prefixing of rule ids is later required, it needs a mapper change (out of scope here).
unmappable_concepts.SENSORS omitted (0 authored): Per FEAT-002 step 12: a SENSOR requires a real executable `command` (mapSensor/validateBlockInput), and the fork ships no sensor script. BMAD's deterministic checks (byte-level shasum freeze verification, full-suite E2E green) are therefore modeled as RULES (project.md 'protected paths / frozen baseline', phase-construction.md 'frozen baseline holds through the loop') plus STAGE reviewer gates (bmad-prd-reviewer-agent, bmad-architecture-reviewer-agent) and party-mode review stages, NOT as Sensors. This is the acceptable fallback the step calls out.
unmappable_concepts.batch/loop runner (run_loop.py / KiroCre: Explicitly excluded by the user ('loop 不用了'). No block, stage, skill, or rule references the loop runner; the dev-loop stages are authored as plain per-unit stages (for_each unit-of-work) with no batch orchestrator.
